TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRIFatal.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (IRIREF: "The resulting IRI MUST comply with the syntactic restrictions of generic IRI syntax"); RDF 1.2 Concepts 3.3 (an IRI "is a string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987"); RFC 3987 2.2 (iauthority = [ iuserinfo "@" ] ihost [ ":" port ], port = *DIGIT)
TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRIFatal.note: <http://www:example.org/> has a non-digit port, so it is not an IRI under RFC 3987 generic syntax; core accepts it (also in N-Triples). RDF4J rejects (ParsedIRI).

TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRINonFat.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (IRIREF: "The resulting IRI MUST comply with the syntactic restrictions of generic IRI syntax"); RFC 3987 2.2
TurtleParserTest#testUnparsableIRINonFat.note: lenient parse keeps the statement with <http://www:example.org/> (2 quads); RDF4J drops it (1 quad). Same root cause as testUnparsableIRIFatal.

TurtleParserTest#testDirLangStringNoLang.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (PNAME_LN: "The namespaces map MUST have a corresponding namespace"); RDF 1.2 Concepts 3.4 ("If and only if the datatype IRI is ...rdf:dirLangString, there is a base direction"; likewise a language tag)
TurtleParserTest#testDirLangStringNoLang.note: the input uses rdf: without declaring it; RDF4J's default NAMESPACES setting (RDFa 1.1 initial context plus others) predeclares it, core rejects (undefined prefix). RDF4J also turns "Hello"^^rdf:dirLangString (no language tag) into an xsd:string literal, which the Turtle term constructor (datatype taken from the iri) does not do.

TurtleParserTest#testNestedTripleTerm2.spec: RDF 1.2 Turtle 7.2 (PNAME_LN: "The namespaces map MUST have a corresponding namespace")
TurtleParserTest#testNestedTripleTerm2.note: the input uses xsd:int without declaring xsd:; RDF4J's default NAMESPACES setting predeclares it, core rejects (undefined prefix: xsd).
